items.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019
items.q: There was one class you took for four years, three hours from nine to noon, with this wonderful teacher by the name of Claude Rose. He’s dead now. But it was four part contrapuntal harmonic technique. And so I got an awful lot out of that.

ctx.x: He would sing “Annie’s cousin Fanny” and those kind of tunes. I hated the gig but it was paying my way through school. But I was working five nights a week and carrying — I did four years, it would have took five years, and playing that gig too. But the music, I already knew most of that stuff man. Some of the teachers would come ask me stuff you know. And so the music study was easy except for I did learn an awful lot about counterpoint and stuff like that. And you know that drilling, every day, every day. There…

say I can get a job finished you know what that’s from? Having to play a senior recital to graduate. So I spent that whole year, my whole senior year, practicing for that recital. I played a Bach French suite, six movements, I played a Hindemith sonata, and a Chopin ballad. And so I was practicing for the whole year and then playing that concert and getting through it successfully enabled me to get a job finished. So like when I came to New York doing stuff like writing those arrangements, I can get the job done.
